description: Hi I'm the team leader, Jana Abu taqa
summary: Lunar Finds is a project aimed at the evolution of the effciency of space missions. Lunar finds aims to provide a website with the same accuracy and effeincy as official NASA tools while having th esimplicity of a story. It showcases a tool called Selenova. Selenova is a tool that translates complicated data from one of NASA's biggest data bank, Horizons, with LOARA to create an animated presentation of this humungous data set to provide the resrearcher with the best top 3 options of landing according to the objectives and conditions of the user, and it provides details about those three locations with pros and cons for all. This tool sucessfully combines accuracy and simplicity and acts as a bridge between both. Additionally, it provides unique features that enable the user to calculate an accurate estimate of the time they would need to move from one point to another on a lunar object, and it provides the firstly safest secondly fastest path to go between those two regions.
details: Lunar finds provides a tool, called Selenova, that translates complicated data banks into a simplified website that provides the conditions and all the data the user might need or ask for to carry out his mission. It is made to be not only limited to top tier engineering teams and doesnt require humongous amounts of money instead its a free website, simple enough for normal citizens even studnets to use. other than its range user bank it also includes unique features such as the escape velocity, time needed, budget, and duration to move from and to sites on a specific moon. We used the sources provided by NASA itself such as Horizons and LOAR to use as our data base for this project, as for the coding it was done by a mix of human intellectual coding and international intellgent assitnace for the codes. Our project's creativity lies in the fact of its simplicity but ability to tell what the most complex softwares cant. Our team considered multiple factors of atmospheric refraction, gravitaional pull of specific plantes and lunar objects, escape velocity factor, and the fact that lunar objects woul have some obstacels while moving from one location to another.
